Loading states: done, working, will exist

A proposal for one vocabulary across the report, for review before anything is built. Real theme CSS is inlined from the tree; only the bn-ghost and bn-skeleton rules and the page chrome are new. Brief: docs/design-loading-states-brief.md.

Artefact: real pixels, as they would ship Commentary: not the product

Why. In testing, progressive display read as broken: people did not see that analysis was still running, and never discovered that the bars under a session are a scrubbable timeline, because they only appear once frames exist. Today the one loading cue is the text shimmer. Skeleton and ghost are not defined anywhere in the system, and design-progressive-lenses.md §2 says “never a skeleton” and “a waiting row shows no thumbnail placeholder”. This page proposes reversing both.

1 · The vocabulary

Three states, five shapes. Switch to Off above to see the static fallback: the working state must still differ from the ghost without motion, so a skeleton is a solid fill and a ghost is a dotted outline.

  • Working is the ghost, started. The same element keeps its shape and position: the dotted outline goes, the fill firms up, the sweep runs. Nothing is swapped in. The sweep is a translucent ink tint laid over whatever fill is there, at a third of the text shimmer’s contrast (2.7% against 20%), because a big slab of pixels turns the same swing into a flash.
  • Text that exists keeps the shipped shimmer. A box with no ghost of its own takes the skeleton. That split keeps §4.7.1 intact and gives block shapes their own rule.
  • Ghost below about 12 px on a side takes fill only (sparkline bars, the 4.5 px strip). A dotted outline turns to noise at that size.
  • Static fallback needs no new gate: the skeleton uses the same two gates as the text shimmer (reduced motion, and the “Show animation while analysing” toggle).

  • A readable row is not a placeholder. Row 1 keeps today’s play box and its closed strip, which draws as soon as the row is readable. Only rows still waiting for ingest carry ghosts.
  • One shimmer per row, as now. The filename is the “working” cue; the other cells wait as ghosts. Nothing else moves.
  • Speaker count is unknown, so one ghost badge, not two.
  • A waiting row is not a disabled one. Muted text stays; the dotted ghosts say “reserved”.
  • The ghost badge and sparkline bars are cell-level and cost nothing to reverse.

  • Row 1 done. Row 2’s strip is the one being drawn now, so it is the only strip that sweeps. Row 3’s is queued, so it is a static ghost.
  • The state machine is real: ghost = scheduled, skeleton = the job is on this session, done = it landed.
  • The placeholder lives in the strip’s own box (same gutter, same track), so when it resolves nothing moves.

3 · How long would a placeholder actually be on screen?

ThingWhen it is produced todaySo the placeholder is up for
ThumbnailAt render (s12_render/report.py). The design doc plans a grab right after ingest, not built. Measured when it is built: 0.14 s per frame, about 1.5 s for ten files. The whole run today: minutes. A skeleton here would shimmer for minutes, which is wrong; a static ghost is right. If extraction moves to ingest, it is seconds and may not need a placeholder at all.
Closed stripNeeds the session’s turns and scene colours. Scene colours are computed per session in the chain (about 1.5 s per hour of video). The closed strip draws as soon as the row is readable, so it needs no placeholder on a readable row. None once readable. A waiting row has no strip yet.
Hover frames and scene stripA background job in serve after the report is readable. It decodes at 4 fps, defers while a run is in progress, and works through sessions one at a time (server/scene_strips.py). Per session, a real wait on long recordings: this is the one place a working shimmer is earned. Decode time per hour of video is not measured; do that before choosing.

6 · Proposed tokens

Defined in this page only; tokens.css is untouched. Timing is reused from the shimmer tokens, not copied.

:root {
    /* Will exist, not started — a STATIC ghost. Quiet outline, quieter fill. Never moves. */
    --bn-ghost-line: var(--bn-colour-border-hover);
    --bn-ghost-outline: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bn-ghost-line) 45%, transparent);
    --bn-ghost-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bn-colour-badge-bg) 45%, transparent);

    /* Working on it now — a BLOCK skeleton. Same character as the text shimmer (single hue,
       same timing, same band), drawn on a box because background-clip:text has no box to clip.
       Polarity follows the theme: the band moves toward the ink, so it darkens on light and
       lightens on dark. */
    --bn-skeleton-base: var(--bn-colour-badge-bg);
    /* A third of what a block of pixels would take from the text shimmer's 20%: on a big slab
       the same swing reads as a flash. The peak is a translucent ink tint laid OVER whatever
       fill the element already has, so a ghost shape and a skeleton box share one sweep. */
    --bn-skeleton-contrast: 2.7%;
    --bn-skeleton-peak: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bn-colour-text) var(--bn-skeleton-contrast), transparent);
    /* Small shapes (sparkline bars, the 4.5px strip) have too little area for the eye to catch
       a third-contrast sweep: they take the earlier, stronger value. */
    --bn-skeleton-contrast-small: 8%;
    --bn-skeleton-peak-small: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bn-colour-text) var(--bn-skeleton-contrast-small), transparent);
}

/* Ghost: 1px dotted outline (1px dots) + faint fill. Shapes under ~12px on a side (sparkline bars, the 4.5px
   strip) cannot carry a dotted outline: they take the fill alone (.bn-ghost--solid). */
.bn-ghost {
    box-sizing: border-box;
    border: 1px dotted var(--bn-ghost-outline);
    background: var(--bn-ghost-fill);
    border-radius: var(--bn-radius-sm);
    cursor: default;
    pointer-events: none;
}
.bn-ghost--solid { border: none; background: var(--bn-ghost-line); opacity: 0.55; }

/* Skeleton: a solid base fill at rest (so the static fallback still differs from a ghost:
   solid vs dashed), with the sweep on top when both motion gates pass. */
.bn-skeleton {
    box-sizing: border-box;
    background-color: var(--bn-skeleton-base);
    border-radius: var(--bn-radius-sm);
    cursor: default;
    pointer-events: none;
}

/* Same two gates as atoms/shimmer.css: reduced-motion, and the app's animation toggle. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    :root:not([data-analysis-animation="off"]) :is(.bn-skeleton, .is-working) {
        background-image: linear-gradient(
            var(--bn-shimmer-angle),
            transparent 0%,
            transparent calc(50% - var(--bn-shimmer-band) / 6),
            var(--bn-skeleton-peak) 50%,
            transparent calc(50% + var(--bn-shimmer-band) / 6),
            transparent 100%
        );
        background-size: 300% 100%;
        background-repeat: no-repeat;
        animation: bn-skeleton-sweep var(--bn-shimmer-period) var(--bn-shimmer-easing) infinite;
        /* Independent phase, so neighbours read as individual organisms, not a strobe. */
        animation-delay: var(--bn-skeleton-phase, 0ms);
    }
}
@keyframes bn-skeleton-sweep {
    0%     { background-position: 100% 50%; }
    66.67% { background-position: 0% 50%; }
    100%   { background-position: 0% 50%; }
}

/* The principle: working is the SAME element as the ghost, started. It keeps its shape and
   position; the dotted outline (the "not started" mark) goes, the fill firms up, the sweep runs.
   Shapes with no outline (sparkline bars) firm up by opacity. */
.bn-ghost:not(.bn-ghost--solid).is-working { border-color: transparent; background-color: var(--bn-skeleton-base); }
.bn-ghost--solid.is-working { opacity: 0.8; }
.bn-ghost--solid.is-working, .bn-tapestry-preview .is-working { --bn-skeleton-peak: var(--bn-skeleton-peak-small); }

/* A thumbnail slot that is not (yet) a thumbnail: no pointer, no play icon. */
.bn-video-thumb.bn-ghost, .bn-video-thumb.bn-skeleton { cursor: default; }

/* The strip's placeholder lives in the strip's own box, so nothing moves when it resolves. */
.bn-tapestry-preview.is-placeholder { cursor: default; pointer-events: none; }

7 · Principles

  • Three states, always the same three. Done; working now; will exist.
  • Shimmer is for something happening to this element now. At most one per row or section; independent phase; never on a thing that is only queued.
  • A ghost only for something we know will arrive. Probe-confirmed video, yes; audio-only, never; a cloud file not downloaded, never.
  • Every placeholder has an exit. Stop removes them; failure resolves to the fallback; nothing shimmers forever.
  • Text that exists keeps the text shimmer; a box with nothing in it gets a skeleton.
  • Not clickable, not focusable, hidden from assistive tech. The region carries aria-busy while work is under way.
  • No words by default. The shape says “coming”.
  • Reserve the real size. A placeholder occupies the box the content will, so arrival never reflows.

8 · Decisions wanted

  1. The deferred scene strip and hover frames: the closed strip is already real on a readable row, so the open question is only whether the later frames earn a placeholder (track alone, or dim generic segments).
  2. Themes ghost: silent, or one plain line of copy?
  3. Thumbnails: extract in the readable chain, as the design doc plans (seconds, so a readable row never needs a thumbnail ghost). Leaving it at render would mean a minutes-long ghost, which I would not ship.
  4. Measure the strip job per hour of video before deciding whether a per-session working shimmer is earned or just noise.
  5. Reverse the 12 Oct rulings (“never a skeleton”, “no waiting-row placeholder”) in design-progressive-lenses.md §2.
  6. Contrast of the ghost outline (--bn-colour-border-hover) is deliberately low; confirm it is visible enough on your screens in both palettes.
